summary: 38625669 (18 placebo-controlled RCTs, 331 healthy active adults, BCAA 3.15-29.3 g/day for 1-28 days) found large reductions in delayed-onset muscle soreness at 24-96 h after muscle-damaging exercise, mixed creatine-kinase effects and no LDH effect. Dr. Pham's decision is a source-content hold only, now resolved for this soreness-recovery scope; the overview and athlete review show no performance or body-composition benefit, which is recorded as a limitation. Fourth-ruling boundary applied: credit limited to exercise-related muscle soreness; strength, endurance, performance and muscle-growth positioning excluded; outcome hierarchy set to not_reported (no designated primary).

applicability.studied_population: Healthy active adults, mostly young men, taking a complete BCAA mixture around muscle-damaging resistance or endurance exercise; the supported finding is less delayed-onset muscle soreness, not muscle growth or performance.

identity.preparation: Oral BCAA mixtures (leucine:isoleucine:valine, mostly 2:1:1 per Table 3) versus placebo

population.description: 18 RCTs (6 crossover, 12 parallel), 331 healthy active participants (14 male-only, 2 female-only, 2 mixed studies) undergoing resistance (13) or endurance (5) muscle-damaging exercise.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression of placebo-controlled RCTs; PICO outcomes CK, LDH and DOMS; 13 high- and 5 acceptable-quality studies (SIGN).

outcomes.name: Delayed-onset muscle soreness: no effect immediately (g -0.28, p=0.259); reduced at 24 h (g -1.34, 95% CI -1.93 to -0.74), 48 h (g -1.75), 72 h (g -1.82), all p<0.001, and 96 h (g -0.82, p=0.008); I2 62-85% except 96 h
Creatine kinase lower immediately (g -0.44, p=0.006) and at 72 h (g -0.99, p=0.002); not at 24, 48 or 96 h
Lactate dehydrogenase: no effect at any time point

limitations: Small trials (331 participants in total), mostly young men; DOMS heterogeneity moderate to high (I2 62-85% at 0-72 h).

Soreness and muscle-damage biomarkers are not evidence of muscle growth, strength, performance or body-composition benefit; declared reviews 38241335 (abstract only) and 36235655 report no effect on performance recovery and negligible performance/body-composition benefit.

Meta-regression associations of higher daily/total dose and longer supplementation with larger effects are observational across studies, not a randomized dose threshold; some daily doses were estimated from mean body mass (Table 3 footnote).
Applies to complete BCAA mixtures, not isolated leucine.
